Traupman 165, 290
M-O s.v. chemistry (Stumpf 1752; Pharm. Austr.)

1chēmicus: long e (Traupman 165 leaves it unmarked). Greek χημεία, with eta; Morgan–Owens s.v. chemistry writes chêmicus (= chēmicus).

chēmicus1, chēmica, chēmicum

declension

The word of the early modern scientists (ars chēmica); chemistry is chēmia or chymia, a chemist chēmiae perītus (Traupman 165). Neither is ancient: Lewis & Short has neither word.

Other words

  • chēmia, chēmiae f. — chemistry

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · Traupman 165

  • chēmiae perītus — chemist (a scientist)

    also used · modern · Traupman 165

See also chemical, science.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 165, 290. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. chemistry.

Lewis & Short has no entry for chemicus.

Lewis & Short: peritus
